sources.entry: ftop - Floating system monitor for Apple Silicon that adapts its layout to any window size, showing per-core usage and frequency, GPU, memory pressure, and network. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Nongfsq/ftop) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]
ftop - Floating system monitor for Apple Silicon that adapts its layout to any window size, showing per-core usage and frequency, GPU, memory pressure, and network.

summary.one_liner: ftop is a floating, resizable system monitor for Apple Silicon Macs showing per-core CPU usage and frequency, GPU, memory, network, power, temperature, and top processes.
summary.what_it_does: It presents current system state in a single native floating panel whose layout adapts to any window size, with no history graphs or disk panels. Per-core usage and frequency are grouped by core type, with GPU shown in its own column alongside memory in use and watts. Memory panel shows used, total, compressed, swap, and system pressure level, while network shows current download and upload speed. A process list shows the busiest apps with icons, folding helper processes into their parent app, and a click opens a card with CPU, memory, and helper details. A menu bar item can show up to three readings (CPU, memory, GPU, download, upload, or power), and settings are available both in the UI and in ~/.config/ftop/config.json5. Hidden or fully covered, it stops reading most metrics to reduce cost.
use_cases: monitor CPU and GPU load while a local model or build runs
see which app is using the most CPU or memory on a Mac
keep a small always-on-top system stats window on the desktop
check per-core usage and frequency on Apple Silicon
show CPU, memory, or network speed in the menu bar
diagnose which hardware readings are available on a Mac
how_to_run: ftop toggle # hide or show it
sudo ftop grant # optional: allow viewing system processes
ftop doctor # check which readings are available
notable: Layout adapts to any window size, so nothing is clipped and no space is left empty
Process list resists jitter: rows move slowly and rank swaps are smoothed
Unavailable readings are shown as unavailable rather than zero
Optional setuid root helper (sudo ftop grant) enables system process visibility
Self-updating from release downloads, with options to notify or never check
caveats: Apple Silicon only and requires macOS 15 or later
Per-core frequency and temperature rely on private macOS interfaces that may break with macOS updates, so it cannot be distributed through the Mac App Store
Seeing system processes requires granting a setuid root helper with sudo
keywords: see what is using my cpu
monitor mac while running local model
